title: The Vietnam War: from anti-colonial struggle to American war
examples: Why did the USA fight in Vietnam?
Why did the USA lose the Vietnam War?

events.label: Gulf of Tonkin
events.ask: Why did the USA fight in Vietnam?

explain.say: On 2 September 1945, in Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh declared Vietnam independent from France, and he opened by quoting the American Declaration of Independence: all men are created equal. Thirty years of war followed, against France and then the United States. Look at the timeline. How did an anti-colonial war become a Cold War war?

draw.text: The Vietnam War: from anti-colonial struggle to American war

events.label: Gulf of Tonkin
events.ask: Why did the USA fight in Vietnam?

explain.say: Now the map. France lost at Dien Bien Phu in 1954, and the Geneva conference split Vietnam at the 17th parallel, with elections promised for 1956 that never happened. The communist North backed fighters in the South, the Viet Cong, along the Ho Chi Minh Trail through Laos and Cambodia. Why route supplies through neighbouring countries?

See the two views. American leaders believed the domino theory: if one country fell to communism, its neighbours would follow. Vietnamese communists saw a war to free and reunite their country. Many South Vietnamese fought hard against communism too. After the Gulf of Tonkin incident in 1964, US troops grew to over half a million. Can both views be true at once?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: A Cold War battle and a war of independence.

explain.say: In January 1968, during the Tet New Year holiday, communist forces attacked cities across the South. They lost militarily, but Americans watching at home lost faith in victory. Look at the sizes, all estimates: perhaps two million Vietnamese civilians died, over a million northern fighters, about 250,000 South Vietnamese soldiers and 58,220 Americans. Each was a person.

draw.text: Estimates vary widely; Vietnam's government gave these in 1995.

explain.say: Why did the USA fail? See the causes: guerrilla warfare, the Trail, Soviet and Chinese supplies, weak governments in Saigon and protest at home. US forces left in 1973 and Saigon fell in April 1975. Thoughtful work. Exam tip: include Vietnamese decisions, not only American ones; historians like Lien-Hang Nguyen have shown Hanoi's own debates.

faq.q: Why did the USA fight in Vietnam?
faq.a: US leaders believed in the domino theory, that a communist victory in Vietnam would spread communism across South-East Asia, and wanted to contain communism and protect American credibility. They backed the South Vietnamese state created after 1954.
asks: What happened in the Gulf of Tonkin?

faq.a: A wave of surprise attacks by North Vietnamese and Viet Cong forces on cities across South Vietnam from 30 January 1968. It failed militarily, but it shocked the American public and turned many against the war.
asks: Why was Tet a turning point?

faq.a: The Vietnamese communist and nationalist leader who declared independence from France on 2 September 1945 and led North Vietnam until his death in 1969. Saigon was renamed Ho Chi Minh City after 1975.
asks: What did Ho Chi Minh declare in 1945?

faq.q: Why did the USA lose the Vietnam War?
faq.a: Historians point to guerrilla tactics and the Ho Chi Minh Trail, Soviet and Chinese aid, the weakness and unpopularity of South Vietnamese governments, the determination of the North, and declining support at home after 1968.
asks: Could the USA have won in Vietnam?

faq.q: What was the Ho Chi Minh Trail?
faq.a: A network of jungle paths and roads through Laos and Cambodia by which North Vietnam sent soldiers and supplies south. Heavy US bombing never closed it.
asks: Why were Laos and Cambodia bombed?

facts: Ho Chi Minh declared Vietnamese independence on 2 September 1945.
The French were defeated at Dien Bien Phu in May 1954.
